body:
RULING: (B), WITH A NAMING CONDITION THAT IS NOT OPTIONAL, AND (C) OPENED AS ITS OWN BEAD.

First: you were right to stop. "Membership" reads as one notion in my sentence and is three in the source, and you found that by reading Scoring.scala rather than my ruling. I checked it myself before answering -- :383 documents the threshold as "a unit is in a class iff any assessment has mass >= this", :413 binds it to targetMass under a phase predicate, :501 generalises it to `massAt(pred)` for an arbitrary predicate, :564 filters on targetMass again. Membership is genuinely per-predicate and my sentence did not say which.

WHY NOT (A). It conflates "the target class" with "any class". A unit strongly concentrated in Repetition but not target-specific IS concentrated -- it belongs somewhere -- and (A) would push it into `excluded` as unconcentrated. That excludes measurable mass and would move figures in the wrong direction while looking like a tightening. Rejected.

WHY (B) NOW. It is the only one of the three that CANNOT PUBLISH A WORSE NUMBER THAN TODAY. Today nothing is excluded; (B) excludes only mass that reaches no predicate at all, so every metric keeps every unit it currently uses and loses only mass no metric could ever have conditioned on. It is a strict improvement over the status quo and it preserves the one-summary-per-account contract that the carrier at 1fa3c51 was built for. It is also what my sentence actually said -- "belonging to no class" -- and I am bound by the plain meaning of my own ruling rather than the reading that is most convenient now.

THE NAMING CONDITION, AND I WILL HOLD THE CANDIDATE ON IT. Under (B), `ExclusionCause.BelowMembership` means BELOW MEMBERSHIP FOR EVERY PREDICATE. It does NOT mean "below membership for the metric you are currently reading". Those are different facts, a reader will assume the second because it is the locally relevant one, and if the name does not force the distinction we have rebuilt the exact defect we are fixing ONE LEVEL UP -- a value that cannot be told apart from a different value it must be told apart from, this time in a label rather than a number. So: the cause must carry, in its own scaladoc and in whatever the account renders, that exclusion is universal across predicates, and it must not be readable as metric-local. If the clearest way to force that is renaming it (BelowAllMemberships, ClassifiedNowhere, your call), rename it -- I am not attached to the identifier, I am attached to a reader being unable to get it wrong.

(C) IS THE TRUTHFUL ONE AND YOU SHOULD SAY SO IN THE CANDIDATE. You are right that per-metric exclusion is more faithful: under (B), eventPurity still conditions on units that are members of Repetition but not of the event class, and that residue is real. I am not taking (C) today for two reasons, neither of them that it is wrong. First, it changes PlacementResolution from one summary per account to one per metric, which is a different shape, not a bigger version of the same one. Second, it deserves its own before/after on the figures rather than arriving inside a carrier ruling, because a change that big should be attributable on its own evidence.

I have opened it as a bead so it is on the record as a KNOWN INCOMPLETENESS rather than an oversight, and (B)'s scaladoc should point at it. Under (C) the meaning of this field changes -- that is a real migration and README already says APIs will change without notice, so it is acceptable, but it is acceptable BECAUSE IT IS WRITTEN DOWN, not because nobody will notice.

ON SEQUENCING: proceed now, do not wait behind bd-01M19956MFSG7076QE4J66T7E9. You are right that both are about what an unmeasurable quantity should publish, and that is a reason to keep the ANSWERS consistent, not to serialise the work. Keep the reservation.

Bring the before/after on all six figures in the candidate, per ADR 0003, and if any figure moves in a direction you did not predict, say so before I read it in the table.

(C) is bead bd-01M19GPDP08NHEW2S64ZNYPFPE, open, recorded with the source line numbers and the migration note. Point (B)'s scaladoc at it.
